title: Halting After a Choice
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, let an oracle and input bit string be fixed, and let $G$ be a predicate on configurations. If the instruction at control state $l$ chooses between $l_1$ and $l_0$, then for either choice bit $b$, halting within the stated bound from the configuration at $l$ implies halting within one fewer step from the selected successor configuration. Here the halting condition requires every choice sequence of the specified length to end in a halted configuration and every earlier live configuration to satisfy $G$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ is a choice between $l_1$ and $l_0$
The configuration at $l$ satisfies the halting condition for $N+1$ steps
